From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@medicorehealth.com>

Cc: Bob Lane <bob.lane@medicorehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security and DPA questions ahead of procurement

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement is asking us to get the security/privacy artifacts in order before we kick off an SOW. Two quick asks from our side to keep the timeline (we'd like to get a PO in place by 5/21):

- Can you share the latest DPA draft and an annotated subprocessor inventory that lists which subprocessors handle telemetry/metrics vs. customer PII?
- We need a simplified dataflow diagram showing where PII enters the system, what components (LLM proxy, KV cache, telemetry pipeline) touch the data, and where keys are stored.

Also, are there any subprocessors that will cross-border transfer IP/PII outside the US? If so we need the transfer mechanism noted.

If you can send what you have today we can loop in procurement and legal to start redlines.

Best,
Alice
Director, Compliance
MediCore Health

Hi Alice —

Great to hear procurement is moving fast. Attaching our current DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_Draft_v3.docx) and a starter subprocessor inventory (subprocessor-inventory.csv). I've also included a short annotated SSQ workbook with suggested answers for the items you flagged — see tab "PII flow (annotated)" in the attached MediCore_SSQ_annotated.xlsx.

Quick notes:
- Subprocessors that may process telemetry (metrics/logs) are marked in the inventory. Any component that can see raw request text is highlighted.
- Cross-border transfers: our hosted runtime may route to EU or APAC regions depending on customer config; default demo/org in your account will stay in US unless you request a GEOfence. We will call out the transfer mechanisms in the DPA annex.
- Key custody: KMS for customer keys is explained in Section 5; optional customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) is available for Dedicated/Private.

Next step: I'd like to run this by our legal team for quick redlines (particularly on retention & telemetry), and then we can push a version to DocuSign. Rishi — can you validate the dataflow diagram? I can draft a simplified PNG if helpful.

Camila

Camila —

Thanks for the packet. I reviewed Redwood_DPA_Draft_v3 and have the following high-level asks before we hand to the customer:

1) Cross-border transfers: add explicit clause referencing SCCs (EU) and appropriate transfer mechanisms for APAC; include a short table in Annex A listing which subprocessors may transfer outside the US and under what legal basis.

2) Telemetry & retention: tighten retention caps for derived telemetry tied to prompt snippets — propose max 90 days for telemetry containing PII unless customer opts-in to longer retention for debugging. Add a mechanism for purge requests and proof-of-deletion (log evidence).

3) Subprocessor evidence: procurement will want proof that CloudPartner Inc. and TelemetryOps have SOC2+ contracts with limited access. Please attach certs or a third-party attestation link.

4) Dataflow diagram: the diagram needs to explicitly show where KV caches store ephemeral context and whether those caches are persisted to disk or encrypted in-flight. Rishi: can you produce a one-page diagram with those boxes called out? I recommend we produce two versions: one simplified for procurement and one technical for security.

I've attached a redline (see: Redwood_DPA_Redline_v3-laura.docx) with proposed language, and a short suggested annex text for the retention/telemetry portion. If we accept these redlines we can push to DocuSign and include an annex listing the requested subprocessor evidence.

Timeline suggestion: legal review completed Tue 5/12, updated DPA to customer Wed 5/13, DocuSign + SSQ requested signature by Fri 5/14, PO target 5/21.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
